rationale: The Court is likely to hold that, on this record, Missouri’s failure-to-warn verdict imposes a non-parallel labeling requirement “in addition to or different from” FIFRA because EPA repeatedly concluded a glyphosate cancer warning is not required and may be misleading. Any separate writings would most likely debate how much weight to give EPA’s determinations and whether Wyeth/Albrecht-style “clear evidence” concepts should inform the Bates parallel-duty inquiry in an express-preemption case.
